references.text: This paragraph contains the original instruction from God to make onyx stones with the names of the sons of Israel engraved, as Exodus 39:6 describes the fulfillment of.
Specifically mentions the engraving of the stones as seals with the names of the children of Israel, the same technique described in 39:6.
Describes the gathering of onyx stones as materials for the sanctuary, which were later used in the work described in 39:6.
States that the leaders brought onyx stones for the work of the ephod, which is completed in 39:6.
Mentions onyx stones among the gifts to be gathered for the sanctuary.
The first mention of the onyx stone (shoham) in the Bible, the same gemstone used in the ephod.
Mentions onyx among precious stones, showing the value and significance of the stone.
This verse confirms the requirement for twelve stones with the names of the tribes that was carried out in the source verse.
This is the original command to use the onyx stones and the names that were followed in the source verse.
This shows the eschatological fulfillment where the twelve tribes on the priests' shoulders become the twelve gates of the new Jerusalem.
This verse reveals the theological purpose behind the inscription: to carry the people's name as a memorial before God.
This shows a parallel use of the 'seal' metaphor to mark holy inscriptions on gold objects.
